summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The deterministic gate failed because the custom 2D steady experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w object, while a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and powers. Both input_gate_pass and scientific_gate_pass are false, independently_verified is false, simulation_allowed is false and comparison_valid is false. The paper (W2796297998) is a numerical linear-solver benchmark of LU versus conjugate gradient (CG) solvers inside the HotSpot simulated-annealing floorplanner. Its reported observables are solver CPU run time and speedup, not temperature. For the selected MCNC ami49 case (49 blocks) it reports LU at 1534.41 s versus SSOR-CG at 134.7 s, a ratio of about 11.39. No block coordinates, dimensions, per-block powers, ambient or boundary conditions are published, only a random power density range of 1e5 to 1e7 W/m2. No linked assets or repositories were found, so no source commit or placement assumption applies, and no illustrative input.flp or input.ptrace was generated. This is a custom steady 2D scenario, so there is no transient trace. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation and not a pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace case. No numerical temperature comparison is possible because the paper reports no temperature and no matching location, aggregation, regime or boundary assumptions exist. Any Studio result would not test the paper's run-time claims, since Studio uses a different solver and has no simulated-annealing optimizer or incremental sparse solver. The final verdict is therefore not_2d_applicable with no replication claim. The paper's run-time numbers are reported only as paper-stated values.
limitations: Studio did not run; there is no simulated temperature, floorplan or power output to assess.
The paper reports no temperature observable, so no numerical comparison is valid. Run time and speedup are solver performance metrics, not thermal observables.

The paper publishes no ami49 block coordinates, widths or heights, no per-block powers (only the random density range 1e5 to 1e7 W/m2), and no ambient, package or cooling boundary conditions. The Perl script and random seed are also missing.
The original setup is a simulated-annealing floorplanner with changing placement and an incremental CG solver, which a fixed-placement steady 2D evaluation cannot reproduce.
The model is a 2D HotSpot block resistance model, not a 3D, interposer or chiplet configuration, and it has no transient workload or controller.
No linked assets, repository, source commit or pinned configuration exist, so no source commit or generated placement assumption can be reported.

Evidence quality gaps remain: several evidence items lack valid page or asset locators, the thermal observable lacks a page, unit, location and aggregation, no steady/transient regime is cited, and adversarial code, parameter, config and data checks and independent page review are unresolved.
The gate sets comparison_valid to false; the paper's run-time figures (1534.41 s, 134.7 s, 11.39x) are reported only as paper-stated values and are not replicated or verified.
The mismatches in physical location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions are essential, so only qualitative discussion is justified.

The paper is a numerical linear-solver speed benchmark and reports no temperature, no per-block dimensions or coordinates, no per-block power values, and no ambient or boundary conditions. No complete thermal experiment can be reconstructed from it, so the selected scenario is not steady_2d_relevant.

The optimizer is simulated-annealing floorplanning with a changing placement and a relative-sparse-matrix incremental solver. A fixed-placement thermal evaluation would not reproduce this optimizer or solver behavior.

The model is a 2D HotSpot block thermal resistance model. There is no 3D stacking, interposer or chiplet structure, and no cooling or package specification is published. It is not comparable to chiplet or 2.5D setups.
Block powers come from a random Perl script (power density 1e5 to 1e7 W/m2), so there is no real workload and no transient power trace. There is no controller or reliability analysis.
No paper-derived floorplan, power rows or thermal observable exist, so the Studio floorplan is empty.

Any Studio run would be a separate illustrative construction using bundled package and material assumptions. Its generated coordinates and powers would be kept distinct from paper facts, and its temperatures would not be compared numerically to the paper, which reports none.
The Studio solver is not the paper's HotSpot LU or CG solver and runs no simulated-annealing optimizer, so no replication of the paper's run-time results is claimed.
